newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Gap has not narrowed on Cyprus, says UN envoy.
newsitem.headline: Gap has not narrowed on Cyprus, says UN envoy.

text.p: The gap between the two sides in divided Cyprus has not narrowed but both agree a solution to the protracted problem is needed, a UN Cyprus envoy said on Wednesday.
"I have spoken with both leaders and I cannot say I have narrowed the gap in any way," said Han Sung-Joo, the UN Secretary-General's special envoy on Cyprus.
"But since the purpose (of the visit) was to find and explore areas of potential agreement I am leaving with the hope and conviction that stepped up efforts are necessary," he told a news conference.

The United Nations has been trying for decades, without success, to reunite the island under a federal system. Turkey invaded the northern third in 1974 after a brief coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.
The result was the virtual partition of the island between Greek and Turkish Cypriots.
Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said on Tuesday the situation on Cyprus had deteriorated in the last six months, accompanied by violence not seen since 1974.

Two Greek Cypriots were killed by Turks and Turkish Cypriots during buffer zone protests in August. In September, a Turkish Cypriot sentry was shot and killed, and in October a Greek Cypriot was shot and killed after straying into Turkish-held territory.
The atmosphere between the two communities was marked by increasing distrust and hostility, Boutros-Ghali said in his report.
"I think there is realisation on both sides that a search for a solution is necessary," said Han, who leaves Cyprus on Thursday for contacts in Athens, and then Ankara.
A 1,162 strong UN force has been stationed on the island since 1964 following the eruption of inter-communal violence.
